assignments.name: Final project
assignments.description: Teams of two to four pick one of three tracks. In the AI Investment Committee track, the team acts as the AI steering committee of a real public company, working only from public sources: diagnose the business and its readiness, score a portfolio of use cases, prototype the lead idea, cost out build versus buy, register the risks, and defend a recommendation to the board in December. In Building and Breaking an AI Agent, teams design an agent that supports a recurring business decision, then red-team another team's agent and say exactly where it breaks. In Make $100, teams start an AI-enabled business and earn real revenue. The grade is the insight, not the money: a team that earns nothing and can explain precisely why will outscore one that earns two hundred dollars and cannot.

assignments.name: Homework
assignments.description: Hands-on exercises outside class. Homework 1, Predictions, asks students to autopsy a famous AI prediction (what exactly was claimed, what happened, why it went right or wrong) and then make a checkable prediction of their own, with peer review. Homework 2, Machine Learning Principles, is all in the browser: train a small neural network on churn-shaped data in TensorFlow Playground, train an image classifier and find the photos that fool it, cost out a real AI experiment, and watch a tokenizer turn text into numbers.

assignments.name: Current Topics in AI presentation
assignments.description: Teams of two to four open a class with an 8 to 10 minute briefing: either a deep dive on an AI product launched or piloted in the last six months (the customer problem, data and methods, safety, competition), or a fair, sourced explainer of a live AI debate such as copyright and training data.

assignments.name: Reading and video response memos
assignments.description: One-page responses to a prompt. Memo 1 follows the 3Blue1Brown deep learning series and asks what a trained network actually learned, and what it does when handed pure static.

assignments.name: Quizzes
assignments.description: A short weekly quiz on Canvas covering the prior week, three attempts, no AI unless stated.

assignments.name: Participation and in-class exercises
